entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Postumius Albinus was a Roman politician and general of the 3rd century BC, born into a wealthy equestrian family in Rome, who rose to prominence through his service in the Roman Republic's early struggles against the Sulla faction.

He was elected consul three times, demonstrating his influence and power within the Roman government, and his military campaigns in Italy and beyond, including his victories against the Samnites and the Gauls, showcased his tactical prowess and leadership skills.

Albinus' legacy, however, is also marked by his tragic fate, as he was assassinated in 215 BCE, along with several other prominent Roman figures, in a conspiracy orchestrated by the Cato family.

The 'Albinus' passage in Livy's Ab Urbe Condita remains a valuable source for understanding Albinus' life and career, but its reliability and accuracy have been debated among historians.

The death of Albinus served as a catalyst for the rise of the Cato family, who would go on to shape Roman politics and society in the centuries to come.

This event can be seen as a pivotal moment in the transformation of the Roman Republic into the Roman Empire, as the assassinations of prominent figures marked a turning point in the struggle for power and succession.
